packages.name: cli
notes: psc run --verified now uses the semantic primitive types retained in verified IR: Nat/Int/Bool/String/Unit arguments are decoded by a dedicated ABI layer; generic or structured main signatures remain fail-closed.
Verified CLI elaboration starts from the shared pskernel-admitted Lean 4.34 Init.Prelude environment and fails closed when that fixture cannot be loaded.
psc --verified uses the preferred source -> elaboration -> checked core -> erasure -> compiler IR -> TypeScript -> JavaScript architecture.
Verified mode never falls back to the legacy software checker after an elaboration/erasure error.
The legacy software path remains available without --verified only as a temporary compatibility lane while verified-core coverage expands.
CLI regression now executes a temporary verified project end-to-end through emitted JavaScript and checks Nat main(21) = 42.

packages.name: browser
notes: Browser foundation provides cancellation-aware streaming verification through an injected verifier adapter.
Kernel/module WebCrypto wiring remains outside this foundation until the browser-safe module codec is defined.

packages.name: syntax
notes: Declaration parameters preserve Lean BinderInfo categories: default, implicit, strictImplicit, and named instImplicit.
D-EXPLICIT-PARAMS remains a ProofScript-owned non-empty explicit group; native `{...}`, `{{...}}`, and named `[...]` binders remain Lean-shaped syntax.
The function alias still requires at least one D-EXPLICIT-PARAMS group, so native implicit binders alone do not satisfy the alias rule.
Canonical lowering and exact feature-ownership conformance preserve binder categories rather than translating them into TypeScript generics.
Native Lean theorem declarations are parsed as inherited command heads; only registered ProofScript parameter/separator decoration is claimed by feature ownership.
A bounded inherited Lean tactic-term parser recognizes `by exact term` and `by assumption` without registering a new ProofScript syntax exception.
Inherited Lean tactic syntax now includes a bounded `intro name; <continuation>` form; it is not registered as new ProofScript syntax.

packages.name: pretty
notes: Foundation provides compositional documents, width-aware groups/indentation, and diagnostic rendering.

packages.name: environment
notes: Platform-neutral replay turns pinned lean4export text into a pskernel Environment.
The Node subpath locates/replays the Lean 4.34 Init.Prelude fixture once and returns clones to compiler/editor clients.
Verified compilation requires the shared prelude provider and fails closed if it is unavailable; editor tooling may expose degraded empty-environment behavior separately.

packages.name: checked-core
notes: Structure field-name/index/binder metadata is accepted only after validation against the constructor generated by pskernel; metadata guides source names but has no proof authority.
Checked core now replays constants and inductive declarations in admission order; inductive families are admitted by pskernel's Lean-style inductive checker.
Checked core is the single semantic boundary between elaboration and compilation.
A CheckedCoreModule is constructed only by replaying declarations through pskernel into a cloned base environment.
Compiler/erasure/editor layers may consume checked core but cannot bypass kernel admission or mutate the kernel TCB.

packages.name: meta
notes: Expr metavariables now use pskernel's real Expr and LocalContext rather than only a generic placeholder protocol.
The context records natural/synthetic/syntheticOpaque kind, creation depth, local scope, assignments, recursive instantiation, occurs checks, and kernel-backed validation once assignments are ground.
Ordinary unification never assigns syntheticOpaque metavariables; explicit assignment remains available to tactic/elaboration code.

This is intentionally not full Lean.Meta.isDefEq: level metavariables, delayed assignments, higher-order pattern unification, postponed constraints, local instance synthesis, and transparency-sensitive meta reduction remain later milestones.
First-order application-spine unification is transactional: nested metavariables such as Option ?α can be solved from expected Option Nat, and failed structural unification rolls assignments back.
This remains intentionally smaller than Lean.Meta.isDefEq; higher-order patterns, level metavariables, coercions and postponed constraints are separate milestones.

packages.name: elab
notes: Bounded structural recursion is elaborated by replacing self-calls on direct recursive match fields with pskernel recursor induction hypotheses; no self constant is introduced into checked core.
The current structural recursion subset requires one explicit runtime recursive parameter and a body headed by a match on that parameter.
Recursive calls on the original scrutinee, arbitrary expressions, or non-recursive fields fail closed as non-decreasing.

General Lean termination elaboration, multiple recursive parameters, course-of-values recursion, well-founded recursion, mutual recursive functions, and recursive where blocks remain later milestones.

Direct positive recursive inductive fields are now elaborated by making only the in-progress inductive header visible in a temporary elaboration environment; final positivity and recursor generation remain entirely pskernel responsibilities.
A negative recursive occurrence regression is rejected by pskernel's existing strict-positivity checker, not by duplicated frontend theory.
Fixed-result matches over direct recursive fields supply the pskernel recursor's induction-hypothesis binders internally while source patterns expose only constructor fields.
Verified constructor pattern matching now elaborates to the pskernel-generated recursor, not to a source-level switch.

The current bounded match subset is exhaustive, constructor-only, fixed-result, unparameterized, unindexed, and non-recursive; recursor universe instantiation is derived from the expected result sort.
A reduction regression checks that getOrZero (MaybeNat.some 7) iota-reduces through pskernel to 7.
Constructors are qualified as TypeName.constructor and become ordinary environment constants; existing dependent application elaboration handles constructor calls.
Parameterized and recursive inductives remain explicit fail-closed milestones; pattern matching is not yet enabled on this verified inductive path.
Record literals elaborate to applications of the pskernel-admitted structure constructor, in validated field order; dependent field types are instantiated by the constructor Pi telescope.
Dotted structure field references elaborate to kernel Expr.proj nodes whose type is checked by pskernel.
Non-parameterized v0.6.1 structures elaborate to genuine single-constructor kernel inductives with generated constructor/recursor metadata. Dependent later fields may reference earlier fields.

Verified braced if now follows Lean ite semantics for the bounded Nat relation subset: condition is a Prop built with LE.le/LT.lt plus instLENat/instLTNat, and Nat.decLe/Nat.decLt supplies the checked Decidable witness.
The runtime compiler erases the checked proposition/decider and lowers the already-validated Nat relation to a boolean host condition; the frontend does not reinterpret if as Bool.

The bounded verified notation subset maps Nat +, -, and * directly to the real Lean constants Nat.add, Nat.sub, and Nat.mul after requiring Nat operands/results. Other operators remain fail-closed until general typeclass notation elaboration.
Lean-native `intro` opens a real forall goal, extends LocalContext with the exact binder type/info, elaborates the continuation against the instantiated codomain, and constructs a lambda proof.
`exact`, `assumption`, and `intro` all elaborate to ordinary pskernel Expr proof terms; Kernel.addTheorem remains final authority.
This milestone still has no synthetic tactic goal engine or cursor snapshots; apply/refine/rewrite/simp/typeclass synthesis and multi-goal tactics remain later work.
The public declaration elaborator now returns @proofscript/checked-core, re-admitted through pskernel as the stable compiler boundary.

Non-recursive parameterized inductives now elaborate shared parameters into the pskernel InductiveDecl; constructor copies of shared parameters are implicit, matching Lean constructor use such as Option.some/Option.none.
Expected-type application/reference elaboration can solve inserted implicit constructor parameters for nullary constructors without introducing runtime arguments.
Verified match elaboration now passes admitted shared inductive parameters before motive/minors/major, matching pskernel recursor binder order for non-recursive unindexed parameterized inductives.
Constructor branch field types are obtained only after instantiating the admitted constructor parameter prefix; source patterns do not define constructor field types.

packages.name: tactic
notes: Foundation provides generic exact, assumption, and intro state transitions; kernel proof-term construction remains adapter-driven and outside the TCB.

packages.name: erasure
notes: For checked definitions with exactly one runtime parameter, a used recursor induction-hypothesis local lowers to a verified IR self-call on its corresponding direct recursive field.
The self-call mapping is derived from pskernel recursor structure and checked-core binder opening, not from raw source recursion.
Definitions with other runtime arities do not receive this mapping; any surviving IH use then fails through erased-local checks.
This enables structurally recursive functions over direct recursive ADTs while general/well-founded recursion remains outside the current compiler subset.
Direct recursive constructor fields now remain self-referential verified IR types and compile to ordinary recursive TypeScript tagged unions.
For recursive recursor applications, generated induction-hypothesis lambdas are consumed as checked compiler-internal artifacts and erased; source patterns still bind constructor fields only.
If an erased induction-hypothesis local survives in executable branch code, ordinary erased-local checks fail closed.
Higher-order recursive fields, indexed/mutual recursion, dependent motives, and structurally recursive function compilation remain separate milestones.
Constructor field names/types are derived from pskernel-generated ConstructorInfo, not trusted source-side ADT metadata.
Kernel-admitted simple structures now lower to verified nominal structure IR; constructor applications become record values and kernel projections become named field access.
Structure layout comes only from checked-core metadata that was validated against pskernel-generated constructor metadata.
Structure fields must currently all be runtime-level and independently representable; Type/Prop/dependent existential fields fail closed rather than being flattened unsafely.
Erasure consumes only kernel-admitted checked core, never source AST or the transitional software checker.
Sort/type binders become TypeScript type parameters but are erased from runtime arguments; Prop proof binders are erased entirely; runtime binders remain.
If an erased type/proof local survives in executable code, lowering fails closed.

The first executable verified-core slice supports generic functions, variables, applications, nested lambdas, lets, literals, and a tiny set of Bool/Unit constants; projections/recursors/primitive runtime calls remain later milestones.
Sort 0 / Prop binders are proof-level and erased completely; higher Sort binders become compile-time TypeScript type parameters. Proof terms whose types inhabit Prop are also erased.
Applications headed by Nat.add/sub/mul lower to verified IR intrinsics. Nat.sub remains a distinct intrinsic because JavaScript bigint subtraction does not have Lean Nat saturation semantics.
Checked ite applications over Nat LE/LT propositions lower to verified IR if nodes; the Decidable proof object is erased only after pskernel admission.
Application/ite/intrinsic lowering is isolated in app-erasure.ts so expression erasure remains below the repository source-shape ceiling.
Source-level regression locks the current boundary: simple runtime structures compile end-to-end, while dependent Type/Prop fields remain explicit fail-closed cases.
Source-level MaybeNat regression locks constructor identity across pskernel admission, checked core, verified IR, TypeScript tagged unions, JavaScript factories, and .d.ts output.

Parameterized recursor erasure now consumes the admitted recursor parameter prefix, erases those checked type arguments, and substitutes them into generic constructor field types before emitting match branch bindings.

packages.name: compiler-ir
notes: Compiler IR now has a verified-core lane distinct from the transitional software-HIR lane.
Verified IR separates compile-time type parameters from runtime parameters so dependent/type binders can be erased from JavaScript while retained in TypeScript declarations.
The verified IR is runtime-oriented and intentionally does not reuse kernel Expr as code-generation IR.
Legacy software IR remains temporarily for coverage while verified-core erasure grows to structures, inductives, recursion, primitives, and effects.
Verified IR has explicit Nat arithmetic intrinsics so Lean runtime semantics are represented intentionally instead of inferred from TypeScript operators.

Verified IR preserves ProofScript primitive identities (Nat/Int/Bool/String/Unit); host TypeScript types are selected only by backend-ts. This keeps runtime/ABI semantics out of the backend type representation.
Verified IR now represents Nat le/lt conditions and if branching explicitly after proposition/Decidable erasure.
Verified IR now represents nominal structure declarations, branded record construction, and field projection without carrying Lean kernel metadata into the backend.
Verified IR now has nominal inductive/constructor metadata and explicit constructor-value expressions, independent of pskernel recursor internals.
Verified IR now has explicit tagged-union match expressions with constructor-specific runtime field bindings.
Verified inductives may carry compile-time type parameters; constructor expressions may carry type arguments used only for TypeScript/.d.ts emission.

packages.name: runtime
notes: Foundation implements exact bigint Nat/Int basics, saturating Nat subtraction, UInt8 normalization, and tagged constructor values; broader Lean runtime semantics remain later work.

packages.name: backend-ts
notes: The preferred backend lane now accepts verified compiler IR produced after pskernel admission and erasure.
Compile-time dependent type parameters are emitted as TypeScript generics for .ts/.d.ts while tsc removes them from JavaScript runtime code.
The backend remains untrusted: TypeScript/JavaScript emission cannot affect theorem validity or kernel admission.
The legacy software-HIR emitter remains temporarily for language coverage until verified-core lowering reaches those constructs.
Verified Nat.add/Nat.mul emit bigint arithmetic; Nat.sub emits a single-evaluation saturating expression matching Lean Nat subtraction.
backend-ts is the layer that maps semantic primitive IR types to host types: Nat/Int -> bigint, Bool -> boolean, String -> string, Unit -> undefined.

Verified structures emit as branded readonly TypeScript interfaces; constructor values carry an internal unique-symbol brand so distinct Lean structures do not collapse under TypeScript structural typing.
Verified inductives emit as unique-symbol tagged unions plus value-level constructor factories; constructor values remain nominally discriminated at runtime.
Verified ADT match IR emits a single-evaluation tagged-union switch; branch field bindings come from checked recursor minors and runtime constructor metadata.
Generic verified ADTs emit TypeScript type parameters and generic constructor factories; tsc removes those type arguments from JavaScript.

packages.name: compiler
notes: Compiler orchestration starts at CheckedCoreModule; it has no syntax, parser, language-checker, or elaborator dependency.
The preferred verified path is checked core -> erasure -> verified compiler IR -> TypeScript -> TypeScript Compiler API -> JavaScript/.d.ts/source map.
The compiler is untrusted with respect to theorem validity; pskernel admission has already occurred before this package runs.
The verified compiler now covers construction and elimination of non-recursive unindexed generic ADTs through kernel-admitted constructors/recursors.

packages.name: language
notes: Software checking has dedicated structure, inductive, match, and where modules rather than one monolithic semantic switch.
Acyclic where helpers are predeclared for local scope, type-checked with outer captures, dependency-sorted, and retained explicitly in checked HIR.
Recursive/mutually recursive where cycles fail closed until Lean-compatible termination elaboration is integrated.
Proof acceptance remains a pskernel/elaborator responsibility outside this software checker.
The executable structure subset accepts explicit named fields only; parsed implicit fields fail closed until generic structure elaboration exists.

packages.name: language-service
notes: Editor analysis distinguishes parse success from kernel verification; only pskernel-admitted declarations are labeled verified.
Declaration-level proof state never fabricates tactic goals: verified theorems report closed, rejected theorems report the actual failure, and unsupported declarations report unavailable.
The service reuses the current parser/elaborator and accepts an environment factory for future project/import integration.
Completion, same-document definition, and reference lookup are lexical/declaration editor aids only; they do not participate in elaboration or kernel admission.
Theorem proof-state responses may include an initialGoal derived from the same real header elaboration used by declaration checking; a verified theorem still reports zero open goals.
Initial goal display is contextual editor information only and is not a cursor-sensitive tactic snapshot.

packages.name: lsp
notes: LSP environment loading is delegated to @proofscript/environment/node so editor and compiler share the same pinned Lean 4.34 replay policy.
Every document analysis receives a clone of that admitted environment; the fixture is replayed by pskernel rather than trusted as pre-verified metadata.
If the fixture is missing or replay fails, the server falls back to an empty environment and reports the degraded editor environment through serverInfo instead of weakening proof acceptance.
Project/import environment composition remains a later language-service milestone.
The transport now exposes completion/definition/references backed by the untrusted language-service index; proof verification status remains independently kernel-derived.

packages.name: project
notes: Foundation provides deterministic dependency ordering, cycle/missing-dependency rejection, and an in-memory build cache; npm/config integration remains later work.
Lean 4.34 final removed deprecated in-kernel native reduction; no NativeEvaluator/native-ir kernel extension is part of the compatibility architecture.
npm workspaces are enabled so package-name imports resolve from the single root install; the root lean-ts-kernel remains the TCB package and outer workspaces may depend on it, never the reverse.
docs/PROOFSCRIPT_ARCHITECTURE.md plus scripts/proofscript-architecture-check.mjs define and enforce the canonical verified compiler dependency direction.
The canonical integration regression now compiles multiple pskernel-admitted Nat functions, including a user-definition call, through verified IR to TypeScript/JavaScript.
The canonical verified integration regression now includes a pskernel-admitted structure whose constructor and projection lower through verified IR to branded TypeScript/JavaScript.

The canonical verified integration regression now includes an unparameterized pskernel-admitted ADT and zero-/one-field constructor values compiled through tagged verified IR to TypeScript/JavaScript.

legacySoftwarePipeline.rule: no automatic fallback from verified-core compilation
